title: Mathematical Framework for Seismic Monitoring of Viscoelastic Media
content: The proposed approach is based on a baseline-monitoring strategy, in which seismic data acquired at an initial reference state are used to quantify subsequent temporal variations in the mechanical parameters of the medium. Seismic wave propagation with attenuation is described using the Generalized Standard Linear Solid (GSLS) model implemented through the τ\tau-method, which enables the incorporation of quality factors for both P- and S-waves. The inverse problem is formulated to reconstruct variations in elastic parameters and relaxation times from the recorded wave field. Assuming small perturbations relative to a known reference medium, the nonlinear inverse problem is linearized and subsequently reduced to a system of linear algebraic equations using a finite basis representation of the unknown parameter perturbations. Singular value decomposition (SVD) is employed to analyze the resolving capability of the corresponding operators and the coupling between reconstructed parameters. The numerical analysis demonstrates that the conditioning of the inverse problem significantly affects the localization of parameter perturbations and the degree of parameter coupling. The proposed mathematical framework provides a basis for further development of quantitative seismic monitoring methods for detecting and characterizing temporal changes in viscoelastic geological media.
